questions.stem: If a chord of a circle is equal to its radius, what is the angle subtended by the chord at the centre?
questions.explanation: C is correct. The chord equals the radius, so the triangle formed by the chord and the two radii has all three sides equal — it is equilateral. Hence every angle including the one at centre = 60°.

questions.stem: What is the length of a tangent drawn from a point 10 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 6 cm?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Tangent length = √(d² − r²) = √(100 − 36) = √64 = 8 cm. The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, forming a right triangle with hypotenuse = distance from external point = 10 cm.

questions.stem: The angle subtended by a chord at the centre of a circle is 120°. What is the angle subtended by the same chord at any point on the major arc?
questions.explanation: A is correct. By the inscribed angle theorem, the angle at any point on the major arc = (1/2) × angle at centre = 120°/2 = 60°. (The angle at the minor arc would be 180°−60° = 120°.)

questions.stem: Two circles of radii 5 cm and 3 cm have their centres 10 cm apart. Find the length of their common internal tangent.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Internal tangent length = √(d² − (r₁+r₂)²) = √(100 − 64) = √36 = 6 cm. (External tangent = √(d²−(r₁−r₂)²) = √96 = 4√6 cm — that's a common wrong pick.)

questions.stem: A tangent PQ at point P of a circle of radius 5 cm meets a line through the centre O at point Q, with OQ = 13 cm. Find the length of PQ.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Since OP ⊥ PQ (radius ⊥ tangent), triangle OPQ is right-angled at P. PQ = √(OQ²−OP²) = √(169−25) = √144 = 12 cm. Recognise 5-12-13 Pythagorean triple.

questions.stem: Two chords AB and CD of a circle intersect inside the circle at point E. If AE = 4 cm, BE = 6 cm and CE = 3 cm, find DE.
questions.explanation: C is correct. By the intersecting-chords theorem: AE × BE = CE × DE → 4 × 6 = 3 × DE → DE = 24/3 = 8 cm.

questions.stem: A chord of a circle is at a perpendicular distance of 4 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. What is the length of the chord?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Half the chord = √(r²−d²) = √(25−16) = √9 = 3 cm. Full chord = 2×3 = 6 cm. (3 cm is only half — a common error.)

questions.stem: Angle inscribed in a semicircle is always:
questions.explanation: B is correct. This is Thales' Theorem: an angle inscribed in a semicircle (i.e., the angle whose arms meet the two ends of a diameter) is always 90°. This is a direct-recall SSC favourite.

questions.stem: Two chords AB and CD of a circle, when extended, meet at point P outside the circle. If PA = 8 cm, PB = 3 cm and PC = 6 cm, find PD.
questions.explanation: B is correct. For external intersection: PA × PB = PC × PD → 8 × 3 = 6 × PD → PD = 24/6 = 4 cm. Note the formula uses the full external segment lengths, not just the chord lengths.

questions.stem: From an external point P, two tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle with centre O and radius 5 cm. If OP = 13 cm, find the area of quadrilateral AOBP.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Tangent length = √(13²−5²) = 12 cm. AOBP consists of two congruent right triangles (OAP and OBP). Area of each = (1/2)×5×12 = 30 cm². Total area = 2×30 = 60 cm².
